caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 805 of 2003
lawyer:
Md Fazlul Karim, Senior Advocate, instructed by Md Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record—For the Petitioner. 
Abdus Samad, Senior Advocate, instructed by Md Feroz Shah, Advocate-on-Record—For the Respondent.
parties:
Yusuf Sarder (Md), Waqf Lillah Estate ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Md Hossain Khan ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
Md Fazlul Karim J; This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 7-5-2003 passed by the High Court Division in First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 626 of 1991 dismissing the suit with modification of the impugned judgment and order dated 7-9-1987 of the District Judge, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No. 59 of 1986 to the effect that the property in question is not a waqf property and the waqf administrator is not required to decide the question as directed in the impugned order. 

 2. That the case of the petitioner is that late Mohd Ibrahim was the owner of case land measuring twenty-four kathas two chataks along with other lands and properties, that he died leaving one wife, three sons and two daughters, that Noor Hossain, predecessor of the respondent as son of late Mohd Ibrahim, filed Title Suit No. 3 of 1947 in the Third Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for partition of paternal properties and the suit was decreed in preliminary form on 29-6-1949 and final decree was passed on 6-8-1951, that allotment 'A' land under the decree was given to Mohd Yousuf Sarder, son of Mohd Ibrahim, and allotment "3" was given to said Noor Hossain and other allotments were given to other heirs, that said Noor Hossain and Mohd Yusuf Sarder did not take possession of their respective allotments through Court and continued their possession according to convenience of both. That Al-haj Mohd Yusuf Sarder dedicated the case land from the lands he possessed and allotted to him for the cause of Allah and by an oral declaration before witnesses on 1-7-1976 constituted a waqf namely, Alhaj Yusuf Sarder Waqf Estate with himself as Mutawalli and prepared waqf nama as waqif Mutawalli on 29-3-1978 and got notaries registration on the same date and applied for enrollment on 3-3-1978 to the office of the Administrator of Waqf without serving any notice to co-sharers. Then an objection was filed under section 50 of the Waqf Ordinance. The learned District Judge after hearing both the parties directed the Administrator by his judgment and order dated 7-4-1979 to enroll the waqf estate. Accordingly, on the basis of no objection certificate dated 8-7-1978 from the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka and report dated 18-7-1978 of the waqf inspector and the judgment in the said Miscellaneous Case, the Administrator was pleased to enroll the said waqf estate on 7-5-1979 being EC No. 15719, that the declaration of the waqf was amended by the waqf Mutwalli four times on 2-2-1979, 11-8-1979, 15- 11-1979 and 31-12-1983. That by the third amendment the name of the waqf estate was amended as "Al-haj Mohd Yousuf Sarder Waqf Estate in English and Bengali and the name of the said Waqf estate was mutated in the concerned revenue office of the Government and Dhaka City Corporation, rents and taxes were paid, annual subscription was given to the Administrator and audit was regularly held. The waqif Mutawalli died on 25-6-1984 and, according to the waqf-nama, Tabarak Ali Sikder became the Mutawalli. It is stated in this connection that said Yusuf Sarder, the Waqif, died without any issue. That after the death of waqif the present respondent on 17-10-1984 applied to the Administrator of Waqfs, purportedly under section 50 of the Waqf Ordinance, for cancellation of the enrolment of the said waqf claiming the waqf property as their own and stating that Title Suit No. 27 of 1974 filed by them for declaration of title and recovery of possession of 27 decimals of land out of waqf property was pending. 

 5. That thereafter the present respondent filed Miscellaneous Case No. 59 of 1986 before the District Judge, Dhaka purportedly under section 35(1) of the Waqf Ordinance 1962 against the judgment and order dated 21-2-1986 of the Administrator of Waqf impleading the present petitioner as the opposite party without impleading the Administrator contending, amongst others, that the waqf nama is forged, ante-dated and fraudulently created by the present Mutawalli Tabarak Ali Sikder and that Title Suit No. 27 of 1974 filed by the respondent, his brother and their father praying for declaration of title in respect of 27 decimals of land and recovery of possession thereof was pending and the waqf property is included in the said suit property and so prayed for cancellation of the enrolment. 

 6. The present petitioner contested the claim by filing written objection denying material allegations in the petition of the Miscellaneous Case No. 59 of 1986 and asserting that case land of Waqf was within the allotment 'A' awarded to late Yusuf Sarder in Title Suit No. 3 of 1947 and late Yusuf Sarder has been always in the possession thereof, that Yusuf Sarder during his life time created the waqf estate consisting of 3980 decimals of land and the Administrator of Waqfs enrolled the same on 7-5-1979 after obtaining "No objection certificate" from the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka and report from Inspector of Waqfs and on the basis of the judgment and order in Miscellaneous Case No. 200 of 1978 and that the name of Waqf has even since been mutated in the records of revenue office and Dhaka City Corporation and the waqf estate has been paying rents, taxes and subscription in the office of the Administrator and getting their account audited. 

 8. Mr Md Fazlul Karim, the learned Counsel for the petitioner submitted that the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division committed an error of law in not appreciating that the proceeding of the Miscellaneous Case No. 59 of 1986 purportedly under section 35(1) of the Waqf Ordinance against the order dated 21-2-1986 of the Administrator is coram-non-judice inasmuch as the said order of the Administrator on the application of the respondent for cancellation of enrollment of the case waqf is not an order under section 50 of the Waqf Ordinance. The learned Counsel further submitted that in view of the fact that the previous Title Suit No. 1 of 1994 being for 27 decimals, the rest 12 decimal belonging to the petitioner is the subject-matter of the subsequent suit for partition. The land being the subject-matter of the Waqf Estate, the Waqf Administrator is competent under provision of section 50 of the Waqf Ordinance, the impugned order is not sustainable in law. 

 9. Mr Abdus Samad, the learned Counsel appearing for the respondent, has submitted that the decree in Title Suit No. 1 of 1964 wherein the question as to whether the suit property is a waqf or not has been set at rest by a declaration that the waqf is void and the entire property has been declared to be secular property belonging to the plaintiff-respondent and also directed recovery of possession, as such, the property in question could not be treated as waqf property and thus the decision of the learned District Judge in Miscellaneous Case No. 59 of 1986 under section 35(1) of the Waqf Ordinance is required to be modified and no hearing on the issue is called for.
